strengths: Project aligns with current AIML academic research trends.
Team of 5 enables parallel development across modules.
Rich open-source ecosystem and community resources are available.
bottlenecks: Integration testing between system components needs early milestone validation.
Clear scope definition and feature prioritisation are critical to prevent overruns.

scopeReport.problemStatement: The project aims to design and develop a functional, multi-vendor e-commerce web application that replicates the core user journey of Flipkart, specifically focusing on product discovery, cart management, and order processing, while integrating a lightweight AI/ML module for personalized product recommendations to enhance user engagement.
objectives: Develop a responsive web interface using React.js for the frontend and Python (Django/Flask) for the backend to handle user authentication, product catalog browsing, and shopping cart functionality.
Implement a basic AI/ML recommendation engine using Python (scikit-learn or TensorFlow) that suggests products based on user browsing history and purchase patterns.
Establish a secure database architecture using PostgreSQL or MySQL to store user profiles, product details, and transaction records, ensuring data integrity and efficient query performance.
inScope: User Authentication: Registration, login, and profile management using JWT or Session-based authentication.
Product Catalog: Search, filter, and sort products by category, price, and rating; display product details with images and descriptions.
Shopping Cart & Checkout: Add/remove items, calculate total price, and simulate a checkout process with a mock payment gateway integration.
AI Recommendation Module: A 'Recommended for You' section on the homepage and product pages using a collaborative filtering or content-based filtering algorithm trained on a static dataset.
Admin Dashboard: A basic interface for administrators to add, edit, or delete products and view recent orders.
outOfScope: Real-time Inventory Management: No integration with physical warehouse systems or real-time stock updates from suppliers.
Complex Payment Processing: No integration with real banking APIs (like Razorpay or Stripe live mode); only mock/sandbox payment flows are allowed.
Mobile Native Apps: No development of iOS or Android native applications; the web app must be mobile-responsive only.
Advanced Logistics & Tracking: No real-time courier tracking, delivery scheduling, or reverse logistics (returns) management system.
Multi-language Support: The application will be built in English only; no localization or multi-language support is required.
scopeReport.targetUsers: Students and academic evaluators who need a demonstration of full-stack web development combined with a practical AI/ML application in an e-commerce context.
keyDeliverables: A fully functional web application deployed on a cloud platform (e.g., AWS EC2, Heroku, or Vercel) with a live URL.
Source code repository with clear documentation, including setup instructions, API documentation, and a README explaining the AI model architecture.
A final project report detailing the system design, database schema, AI/ML methodology, and test results.
assumptions: The team has access to a public e-commerce dataset (e.g., from Kaggle) to train the recommendation engine, as collecting real-time user data is not feasible in this timeline.
The 'working module' refers to the core transactional flow (browse -> cart -> checkout) and does not imply a fully operational business with real money transactions.
The AI/ML component is a standalone module that can be tested independently and integrated via API, rather than being deeply embedded into every backend function.
constraints: The project must be completed within 210 days (30 weeks) with a team of 5 students, requiring strict adherence to a phased development schedule (MVP in 10 weeks, AI integration in 10 weeks, testing/deployment in 10 weeks).
The technology stack is limited to Python, JavaScript/React, and a relational database to align with the team's existing skill profile and ensure maintainability.
The AI/ML model must be lightweight enough to run on standard cloud instances without requiring high-end GPU resources, focusing on accuracy over complexity.
